title: Initiative Orbit: Company OKR Convergence & Decision Forecast
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Purpose: establish a lightweight, repeatable playbook that maps company-level OKRs to a prioritized set of cross-functional initiatives (the 'initiative orbit'), produces a decision forecast for the quarter, and exposes clear escalation and handoff points for tactical teams. Background: over the last two quarters we observed inconsistent translation of company objectives into deliverable initiatives; engineering and product teams reported ambiguous ownership and last-minute scope shifts. This ticket is the canonical effort to unify owners, define a compact set of acceptance criteria for initiative readiness, and create a forecasting cadence that integrates with the weekly roadmap sync and executive OKR review. Scope: define the playbook, a decision rubric, a 6-week forecasting template, and an initial pilot run across Platform, Console, and Dedicated capacity initiatives. Out of scope: detailed per-team sprint planning and execution tasks (these remain with each team).
acceptance_criteria: A1: A written playbook (<=6 pages) exists and is approved by product, eng, and design leads that maps OKR lines to initiative boundaries and ownership rules.
A2: A decision forecasting template (spreadsheet + instructions) is created and used in one full planning cadence cycle with at least three initiative owners contributing forecasts.
A3: Two decision escalation paths are defined with named stakeholders and SLAs for responses (technical gating, resourcing conflicts).
comments: 2025-01-13 • Liam O'Connor: Kickoff complete. Collected initial OKR mapping from PMs for infra, console, and dedicated. Noted overlap between 'throughput' and 'cost' initiatives — tracking as potential consolidation.

2025-01-22 • Aisha Patel: Shared first draft playbook to /drive/company/okr-playbook-v0.2. Requested feedback from Design (Maya Li) and Eng (Carlos Reyes). Asked for concrete ownership nominations by 2025-01-29.
2025-02-03 • Maya Li: Proposed UI-specific initiative boundary to keep Console telemetry in a separate initiative; risk that it fragments rollout. Suggest a canary + rollup approach in the playbook.

2025-02-12 • Carlos Reyes: Flagged dependency ENG-1842 (serve runtime batching work) — it must be slotted into the throughput initiative or we risk muddying success metrics. Recommended adding a dependency window in the decision template.

2025-02-20 • Liam O'Connor: Pilot forecast completed for three initiatives. Observations: two initiatives show >30% risk of slipping due to resource contention; scheduled a resource triage meeting for 2025-02-25.
2025-03-02 • Aisha Patel: Incorporated feedback from exec review. Reduced playbook to five decision steps and added 'fallback model' policy for capacity constraints. Updated playbook in links.
decisions: D1: Use a compact initiative boundary model (max 3 deliverables per initiative) to reduce cross-team coupling — approved by product and eng leads.
D2: Forecasting cadence will be bi-weekly for the first quarter of rollout, then reassess; cadence decision balances overhead and signal freshness.

D3: Metric alignment: each initiative must publish a primary leading indicator (throughput, error-rate, latency percentile, or adoption) and one business outcome metric. This is required for roll/gate decisions.
D4: For conflicts where two initiatives claim the same component, the tie-breaker is: (1) customer impact score, (2) alignment to top-level OKR, (3) execution readiness.
next_steps: N1: Finalize playbook v1 and circulate for sign-off by 2025-03-08 (owners: Aisha, Liam).
N2: Run one end-to-end forecasting session with initiative owners and director-level reviewers week of 2025-03-10 (prepare pre-read using template).
N3: Create a lightweight dashboard card in the Console that surfaces the initiative forecast and the top-3 risks (owner: Data Platform).
N4: Feed the pilot learnings into cycle planning and update acceptance criteria by 2025-03-22.
